papers.title: Learning Hamiltonians from Trajectory Data with Kernel Methods
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of a Hamiltonian from discrete trajectory observations using structure-preserving kernel methods. When exact-flow data are fitted through a symplectic one-step scheme, the fixed-step learning target is generally not the physical Hamiltonian itself, but a scheme-dependent inverse modified Hamiltonian. For the implicit midpoint and $p$-implicit symplectic Euler methods, we establish the existence of analytic inverse targets and show that their discrepancies from the physical Hamiltonian are second and first order in the observation step, respectively. Within an RKHS framework, we derive finite-sample reconstruction bounds for random trajectories, allowing dependence among observations from the same trajectory, and separate the error into estimation, approximation, and integrator-induced components. We further establish stability under noisy trajectory observations and develop a multistride Richardson correction that systematically raises the order of the integrator-induced error without requiring additional trajectories. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted scheme-dependent orders, the effect of Richardson correction, and the applicability of the method across several Hamiltonian systems.

papers.title: Irrational families of Fano weighted complete intersection fourfolds
papers.abstract: We study the irrationality of smooth Fano complete intersection fourfolds in weighted projective spaces, using an atom theoretic approach based solely on Gromov--Witten invariants. We prove symplectic irrationality, and hence irrationality for every smooth member, in a wide range of families for which irrationality was previously known only for very general members.

papers.title: Shifted Symplectic Fibrations and Derived Thurston Theorem
papers.abstract: In classical symplectic geometry, under mild conditions, Thurston proved that one can construct a compatible symplectic form on the total space of a symplectic fibration with a connected symplectic base. Here we prove a derived symplectic analogue of this result, called the derived Thurston theorem. More precisely, we show that if a morphism $\pi: X \rightarrow S$ of derived stacks has a shifted symplectic fibration structure and the target stack $S$ admits a shifted symplectic structure, then, under certain conditions, one can construct a shifted symplectic structure on a dense Zariski-open derived substack of the source stack $X$, compatible with $\pi$ in a sense similar to the classical case. In this derived setting, we also present numerous examples of shifted symplectic fibrations, develop an affine model construction for such fibrations, and provide applications of the derived Thurston theorem.

papers.title: Symplectic symmetries of a hypothetical exotic $CP^2$: a potential construction or a nonexistence proof
papers.abstract: This paper is primarily concerned with the existence of a symplectic $4$-manifold, homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $CP^2$, which admits a nontrivial finite order symplectomorphism. We reduced the existence of such an exotic $CP^2$ to a question in contact geometry. More concretely, we showed that there are precisely $12$ plumbed manifolds, each equipped with a canonical contact structure associated to the plumbing, such that an exotic $CP^2$ with a nontrivial finite order symplectomorphism exists if and only if one of the $12$ contact plumbed manifolds admits a certain specific symplectic filling. As the main technical result, we completely determined the order and local representations of a pseudofree symplectic $Z_p$-action for an odd prime $p$ on a rational homology $CP^2$ with positive canonical class. Our result suggests that potentially, there are symplectic $Z_p$-actions which are not a finite automorphism of a fake projective plane. Moreover, we introduced a construction, which, under the minimal assumptions on the symplectic fillings of the $12$ contact plumbed manifolds, produces a symplectic $4$-manifold on the Bogomolov-Miyaoka-Yau line via a reverse-engineering process.

papers.title: Analytic Liouville Integrable Geodesic Flow Has Zero Entropy
papers.abstract: This paper studies the topological entropy of real-analytic Liouville integrable Hamiltonian systems. We prove that the Hamiltonian flow on a compact connected regular energy hypersurface has zero topological entropy whenever a complete family of commuting real-analytic first integrals is generically independent in a connected neighborhood of that hypersurface. The proof uses finite normal expansions along minimal analytic carriers and an ergodic version of Ziglin's leading-term argument to obtain independent invariant normal polynomials, whose Poisson geometry makes all tangent Lyapunov exponents of the carriers vanish. In particular, we prove that a real-analytic Liouville integrable geodesic flow on a closed real-analytic Riemannian manifold has zero topological entropy, giving a positive answer to the conjecture proposed by Paternain in 1992.

papers.title: Yang-Mills Theory in the Multisymplectic Framework
papers.abstract: This Master's thesis develops and applies the multisymplectic field-theory framework to (pure) Yang-Mills theory. Building from the geometric foundations of jet bundles and the Poincar\'e-Cartan forms, the work constructs the Lagrangian multisymplectic formalism for first-order field theories, recovering the usual Euler-Lagrange field equations and extending the Poisson brackets of symplectic mechanics to a full graded Lie algebra. It then establishes the Legendre correspondence with the multisymplectic Hamiltonian formalism (in which Hamilton equations are retrieved) including the case of singular Lagrangians (where a constraint algorithm is reproduced). Breaking Lorentz covariance via a Cauchy surface slicing, the thesis then relates the covariant multisymplectic picture to an instantaneous presymplectic (infinite-dimensional) formulation in which the instantaneous De Donder equations and presymplectic brackets are obtained in a compatible way. A comprehensive treatment of symmetries then leads to multisymplectic and instantaneous momentum maps generalizations and to several versions of Noether's theorems. Specializing the formalism to principal-bundle gauge theory, the thesis identifies the multisymplectic configuration space with the bundle of connections, gauge symmetries with symmetries in the multisymplectic language and builds the Yang-Mills Lagrangian. Lastly, among many computations, the standard tensorial Yang-Mills equations and the Bianchi identity in local trivializations are retrieved, Yang-Mills conserved currents and charges are obtained and the graded algebra is derived for a special class of Hamiltonian forms.

papers.title: Localization of Floer homology for $\mathbb{Z}_p$-actions
papers.abstract: For an odd prime $p$, we prove a Smith inequality over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for exact Lagrangian Floer homology under a symplectic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action, assuming an equivariant stable normal trivialization compatible with the Lagrangians and the required relative Pin data. As an application, we obtain a rank inequality between the symplectic Khovanov homology of a $p$-periodic link and that of its quotient. These results extend the involutive localization of Seidel and Smith. The main construction is a stabilized chain complex. At every invariant intersection point we adjoin the Morse complex of a finite-dimensional normal spectral sphere, whose generators lie in free $\mathbb{Z}_p$-orbits. The differential counts holomorphic strips coupled to sphere half-trajectories by a one-sided weighted asymptotic evaluation. We prove transversality, a uniform spectral cutoff, and the compactification and gluing statements needed for the chain identity. The stabilized complex is quasi-isomorphic to the ordinary Floer complex and contains the complex of the fixed data as a subcomplex with free quotient, so the algebraic Smith inequality applies.

papers.title: Metaplectic-c prequantizations and the Einstein--Brillouin--Keller quantizability condition
papers.abstract: We show that every symplectic manifold admits a symplectic form whose metaplectic-c prequantizations give quantizability conditions on all its Lagrangian submanifolds. Metaplectic-c prequantizations descend to prequantizations over the Lagrangian Grassmannian bundle that are fibrewise flat with holonomies primitive fourth roots of unity on the generators of the fundamental groups. This fibrewise holonomy is consistently interpreted as that of both Leray two-orientations and normalized Blattner--Kostant--Sternberg half-forms. The prequantizations pull back to flat circle bundles on each Lagrangian submanifold whose holonomy character defines a quantizability condition. The first and second Stiefel--Whitney classes are identified as splitting obstructions to the Lagrangianwise holonomies. These holonomies split into a product of holonomies on any orientable Lagrangian submanifold, and split consistently for all Lagrangian submanifolds of a manifold with metaplectic structure. When the first Chern class vanishes, the holonomy splits into the Bohr--Sommerfeld factor and a quarter phase Maslov correction, recovering the classical Einstein--Brillouin--Keller condition. We develop the underlying obstruction theory for circle extensions associated to general Lie group double coverings with first hypercohomology groupoids.

papers.title: Global surfaces of section for dynamically convex Reeb flows on lens spaces
papers.abstract: We show that a dynamically convex Reeb flow on the standard tight lens space $(L(p, 1),\xi_{\mathrm{std}})$, $p>1,$ admits a $p$-unknotted closed Reeb orbit $P$ which is the binding of a rational open book decomposition with disk-like pages. Each page is a rational global surface of section for the Reeb flow and the Conley-Zehnder index of the $p$-th iterate of $P$ is $3$. We also check dynamical convexity in the H\'enon-Heiles system for low positive energies. In this case the rational open book decomposition follows from the fact that the sphere-like component of the energy surface admits a $\mathbb{Z}_{3}$-symmetric periodic orbit and the flow descends to a Reeb flow on the standard tight $(L(3,2),\xi_{\mathrm{std}})$.

papers.title: Braid Stability and a Floer theory of Braid Isotopies
papers.abstract: We build a Floer theory on the space of braids of periodic orbits of a Hamiltonian flow on a closed symplectic surface. The differential and continuation maps are defined by counting Floer isotopies of braids: tuples of Floer cylinders with pairwise disjoint graphs. With this new perspective, we prove a quantitative braid stability result that shows the persistence of braids under possibly large Hamiltonian perturbations. As an application, we show that for every $\alpha\geq 0$ there is a sequence of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms $\phi_k$ on the two-torus $T^2$ such that $$d_H(\operatorname{Ent}_{\leq \alpha}(T^2,\omega),\phi_k)\to \infty \quad (k \to \infty),$$ where $\text{Ent}_{\leq \alpha}(T^2,\omega)\subset \text{Ham}(T^2,\omega)$ denotes the set of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms with topological entropy at most $\alpha$ and $d_H$ the Hofer metric. We prove this result by studying only contractible periodic orbits, whereas analogous higher-genus statements were previously obtained using non-contractible orbits.

papers.title: Bi-contact plugs and dynamical hyperbolicity
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of bi-contact plugs on oriented $3$-manifolds to construct Anosov flows or, more generally, structurally stable nonsingular flows. For a hyperbolic plug with filling Morse-Smale boundary laminations, we prove that every strongly transverse gluing map can be isotoped through strongly transverse maps to identify a strongly adapted unoriented contact form. The resulting flow is hyperbolic and is Anosov when the quotient is closed. This answers a question of B\'eguin-Bonatti-Yu. The result also extends to gluing nonsingular partially hyperbolic flows. Anosov completion by reflection embeds each such hyperbolic plug in an Anosov flow on its oriented double. Further applications include a classification of structurally generic projectively Anosov flows without saddle periodic orbits and Morse-Smale examples with prescribed saddle count. Generalizing the construction of Bonatti-Bowden-Potrie, finite capping embeds any bi-contact plug in a closed projectively Anosov flow with the same topological entropy, preserving partial hyperbolicity for attracting plugs. We also construct flows with controlled invariant torus dynamics on torus bundles and on doubles of plugs with coorientable boundary bi-foliations. Finally, every cooriented partially hyperbolic bi-contact plug admits a Liouville structure on its thickening, with Liouville trajectories projecting to positively reparametrized flow lines. Repelling plugs yield four-dimensional Liouville domains, often with chaotic skeletons.

papers.title: Tight surgeries on torus knots
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of tight contact structures on manifolds obtained from any surgery along any torus knot, which provides the first such classification on an infinite family of knots. The main tools are the classification of non-loose torus knots, bordered contact invariants via their immersed curve interpretations, and non-thickenable tori in knot complements. As a byproduct of this classification, we also give the first classification of contact structures on some surface bundles over the circle with fibers of genus larger than $1$. The symplectic fillability of these contact structures is also studied and leads to, among other things, the disproof of a conjecture of Ghiggini and Van Horn-Morris on Stein fillability of some contact structures on a Brieskorn sphere.

papers.title: Symplectic four-manifolds and hyperbolic $\pi$-orbifolds
papers.abstract: We construct closed symplectic 4-manifolds admitting the structure of hyperbolic $\pi$-orbifold, addressing LeBrun's conjecture. Our simplest example has Euler characteristic $304$, is tessellated by $64$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic $120$-cell and admits a four-fold branched covering over a product of two surfaces of genus $4$.

papers.title: Lagrangian cobordism functor in microlocal sheaf theory I
papers.abstract: Given a Lagrangian cobordism $L$ of Legendrian submanifolds from $\Lambda_-$ to $\Lambda_+$, we construct a functor $\Phi_L^*: Sh^c_{\Lambda_+}(M) \rightarrow Sh^c_{\Lambda_-}(M) \otimes_{C_{-*}(\Omega_*\Lambda_-)} C_{-*}(\Omega_*L)$ between sheaf categories of compact objects with singular support on $\Lambda_\pm$ and its right adjoint on sheaf categories of proper objects, using Nadler-Shende's work. This gives a sheaf theory description analogous to the Lagrangian cobordism map on Legendrian contact homologies and the right adjoint on their unital augmentation categories. We also deduce some long exact sequences and new obstructions to Lagrangian cobordisms between high dimensional Legendrian submanifolds.

papers.title: Deformation quantization of symplectic vector fields
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study deformation quantization of symplectic vector fields \`a la Fedosov. We provide an explicit construction to quantize each symplectic vector field as a derivation of the deformed star algebra. This recovers a result of M\"uller-Bahns and Neumaier with an explicit formula of higher total degree terms. Moreover, we show that this quantization yields a non-abelian $2$-cocycle on the Lie algebra of symplectic vector fields with values in the deformed star algebra. For a Fedosov deformation quantization with vanishing first characteristic class, this non-abelian $2$-cocycle can provide a formal deformation of the crossed-product algebra generated by the action of symplectic vector fields. In this sense, we can quantize any Lie algebra action by symplectic vector fields.

papers.title: Hyperquiver varieties
papers.abstract: We discuss the recently introduced concept of hyperquivers, due to Muller, Nanda, and Seigal, from the point of view of K\"ahler and hyperk\"ahler quotients. In particular, we show that the K\"ahler hyperquiver variety ${\mathcal M}$, corresponding to a hyperquiver with a single hyperedge, is a projective variety isomorphic to the geometric quotient of the space of tensors with maximal multilinear rank. Moreover, the hyperk\"ahler hyperquiver variety corresponding to doubling of this hyperquiver can be identified with the linear scheme corresponding to the sheaf of reflexive $1$-forms on ${\mathcal M}$.

papers.title: Godbillon-Vey classes of Lie subalgebroids
papers.abstract: The Godbillon--Vey class is a secondary characteristic class which is defined for regular foliations and has been studied extensively. In this paper, we fix a Lie algebroid and relatively define the Godbillon--Vey class for its Lie subalgebroids, and study their properties. We also present several examples.

papers.title: Nahm-Kirchhoff Moduli Spaces, Hyperk\"ahler Quotient and 2D Field theories
papers.abstract: To an oriented quiver with boundary $\Gamma$ and a compact connected Lie group $G$ we associate a Nahm-Kirchhoff moduli space $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{H}}(\Gamma)$: solutions of Nahm's equations on the edges with Kirchhoff matching at interior vertices, modulo boundary-trivial gauge transformations. For connected $\Gamma$, $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{H}}(\Gamma)$ is a smooth manifold of dimension $4(|E|-|\Gamma_{\mathrm{int}}|)\dim G$ with a hyperk\"ahler structure arising as an infinite-dimensional hyperk\"ahler quotient. Via a Kempf-Ness argument on the Cartan-Hadamard manifold $G_{\mathbb{C}}/G$, we prove a quiver analogue of Donaldson's theorem identifying it with the complex-symplectic quotient $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{C}}(\Gamma)$ of the complex Nahm equations by the complexified gauge group. This quotient is independent of edge lengths and isomorphic to a finite-dimensional complex-symplectic quotient of $(T^*G_{\mathbb{C}})^E$, while the hyperk\"ahler metric depends on them: uniform rescaling acts by a homothety, and the transported metrics genuinely vary. By cutting and gluing, $\Gamma\mapsto\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{C}}(\Gamma)$ is a 2D TQFT valued in complex Hamiltonian manifolds, \`a la Moore-Tachikawa, whereas the hyperk\"ahler refinement is not functorial on $\mathbf{Cob}_2$: spines of a cylinder with different lengths give non-isomorphic spaces. Retaining lengths, these spaces form a metric field theory, a functor of non-unital monoidal categories from metric cobordisms to hyperk\"ahler manifolds composed by hyperk\"ahler reduction; over each cone of $M_{g,n}^{\mathrm{trop}}$ they give a family with fixed complex-symplectic fibre and varying metric. Finally, harmonic gauge representatives converge as an internal edge collapses, and on a long edge with regular semisimple Higgs field the Kempf-Ness minimizer is exponentially confined near its centralizer; the limiting metrics are left open.

papers.title: Exotic S^2 x S^2 candidates that are just fake
papers.abstract: We show that two infinite families of homology $S^2\times S^2$'s presented in \cite{FPS, AP}, originally proposed as exotic candidates, are aspherical. In particular, none of these manifolds is an exotic $S^2\times S^2$. We prove this by reconstructing them from aspherical building blocks, following Edmonds. The same arguments apply to and rule out further candidates for simply connected exotica. We also give counterexamples to the conjecture that Luttinger surgery preserves symplectic asphericity.

papers.title: Cotangent Bundles as Coadjoint Orbits and Asymptotic Character Formulas
papers.abstract: We present geometric quantization on cotangent bundles as a special instance of Kirillov's orbit method. To this end, the cotangent bundle is realized as a coadjoint orbit of an infinite-dimensional Lie group for a variety of topologies on the dual of its Lie algebra. The group, central to quantum mechanics on manifolds, is the semidirect product constructed from the diffeomorphism group acting on the abelian group of smooth functions on the manifold. We then develop asymptotic character formulas by employing the tangent groupoid of the manifold and investigating the interplay between its groupoid C$^\ast$-algebra and the infinite-dimensional Lie group.

papers.title: A Smooth Hamiltonian Diffeomorphism with Two Fixed Points on $S^2\times S^2$
papers.abstract: We give a construction of a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the equal-area symplectic product $S^2\times S^2$ with two fixed points. The argument starts with a four-fixed-point map, passes to rescaled cotangent coordinates near the antidiagonal, and reduces the local fixed-point equations to two planar saddle problems. A relative modification merges each pair of saddles, and mixed generating functions are used to transfer the modification to the original map. We include detailed explanations of the normal form along a level arc, the Moser equation, uniform existence of mixed generating functions, the order of parameter choices, and the global graph argument. This construction gives a counterexample to the degenerate version of Arnold's conjecture proposed by Arnold\cite{Arnold86} when the manifold is standard $S^2\times S^2$. This work is done with ChatGPT. The author gave the idea to study the limit behavior of $\Phi_\rho$. GPT suggested a key idea of using second generating function to construct this Hamiltonian. Also, most of the computation is done by GPT.
